name: Unemployment: Measurement, Costs, and Types
description: Labor force statistics and the unemployment/participation rate formulas, the economic/psychological/social costs of unemployment, unemployment duration, and the frictional/cyclical/structural typology.

name: Business Cycles, Output Gaps, and Okun's Law
description: Recessions and expansions, potential vs. actual output, the output gap formula, the natural rate of unemployment, and Okun's Law linking cyclical unemployment to the output gap.

name: The Keynesian Cross Model of Short-Run Output
description: Planned aggregate expenditure and its components, the consumption function, solving for short-run equilibrium output, and the income-expenditure multiplier.

name: Fiscal Policy and Stabilization
description: Stabilization policy goals, how taxes and transfers affect spending, supply-side effects on potential output, deficit spending tradeoffs, fiscal policy's flexibility limits, and automatic stabilizers.

name: The Fed, Money Supply, and Money Demand
description: The Federal Reserve's structure and tools for controlling the money supply, the determinants of money demand, and how the money market reaches equilibrium at a given nominal interest rate.

name: Monetary Policy Transmission and the Financial Crisis Response
description: How the Fed's control of the nominal interest rate becomes control of the real interest rate, the channels through which monetary policy affects spending, policy reaction functions and the Taylor rule, and the Fed's unconventional response to the 2008-09 crisis.

name: The AD-AS Model: Equilibrium, Shocks, and Policy Responses
description: The aggregate demand and aggregate supply curves, why AD slopes down and what shifts it versus moves along it, the AS curve's short-run equation and its shifters, short-run versus long-run equilibrium, and how the AD-AS model responds to demand shocks, inflation shocks, and capacity shocks under different policy choices.

name: Inflation Dynamics and Monetary Policy Credibility
description: Inflation inertia and inflation expectations, the self-correcting economy and stabilization-policy tradeoffs, the 1970s-80s Great Inflation and Volcker's disinflation, the post-1980s Great Moderation, central-bank credibility, and the inside/outside lags that limit any stabilization policy.

name: The 2008 Financial Crisis: Mechanics, Response, and Historical Lessons
description: The subprime-mortgage and securitization mechanics behind the 2007-09 crisis, leverage and balance-sheet dynamics, too-big-to-fail and the credit crunch, the Fed's unconventional monetary policy at the zero lower bound, and the fiscal-multiplier and Great-Depression-era policy debates the crisis revived.

name: Exchange Rates and Purchasing Power Parity
description: The foreign exchange (FOREX) market's supply and demand, how it differs from the Fed-controlled money supply, how monetary policy transmits through the exchange-rate channel, nominal versus real exchange rates, the law of one price, and purchasing power parity's long-run predictions and short-run limits.

name: Fixed vs. Floating Exchange Rates and the Policy Trilemma
description: The costs and benefits of fixed versus floating exchange rate regimes, the optimum currency area framework, the open-economy policy trilemma (exchange-rate stability, monetary autonomy, and free capital movement), and capital controls, illustrated through historical currency-crisis case studies.
